note: Retired facts from the game-era build. Nothing on the exhibit page or in src/ references these ids; they were moved out of facts.json in the July 2026 review so the About colophon's source count reflects only works actually behind the page. Each entry keeps the factcheck claim it passed under (embedded as `factcheck`). To revive one, move it back into facts.json and restore its claim to factcheck.json.

facts.display: about 800 men danced through Chicago in August 1835

source.title: Eyewitness account of the 1835 Potawatomi farewell dance
source.author: John Dean Caton
source.locator: recollection published later by Caton, then a young Chicago lawyer

facts.notes: At the last annuity payment about 800 men danced through the streets of Chicago. Caton wrote that the dancers understood it as the last dance on their native soil. Single eyewitness account, so tier attributed.

factcheck.claim: About 800 men danced through Chicago at the last annuity payment in August 1835.
factcheck.note: Single eyewitness account by John Caton, so the fact ships at tier attributed.
factcheck.source: John Caton account via land deep dive stats (lastDancers)

facts.display: 859 Potawatomi forced from Indiana to Kansas in 1838

source.title: Potawatomi Trail of Death records
source.locator: Twin Lakes, Indiana to the Osage River, Kansas

facts.notes: The route ran roughly 660 miles over 61 days. More than forty died on the way, most of them children, of typhoid and exhaustion.

factcheck.claim: In 1838 some 859 Potawatomi were force-marched 660 miles in 61 days; more than 40 died.
factcheck.note: Matches Trail of Death records carried in the deep dive.
factcheck.source: Potawatomi Trail of Death records; land deep dive s5 and stats

facts.display: the first University of Chicago failed in 1886

source.title: Old University of Chicago
source.author: Wikipedia

facts.notes: A Baptist college on ten acres Senator Stephen A. Douglas donated at Cottage Grove and 35th. It struggled with debt for decades and closed in foreclosure in 1886. The new university was a separate legal entity. The deep dive uses an 1857 charter year; the film factcheck kept the 1856 charter framing.

factcheck.claim: The first University of Chicago, on Douglas's donated land, closed in foreclosure in 1886.
factcheck.note: Film verify kept the 1856 charter framing; the deep dive stat uses 1857. The 1886 closing is consistent across both.
factcheck.source: hp-research.json university verify; Old University of Chicago records

facts.notes: The Court dismissed the constitutional challenge to a private covenant, and the real estate industry read the dismissal as a green light. Chicago's covenant wave, including Kenwood, Hyde Park, Woodlawn, Oakland, and Englewood, dates from the late 1920s.
